title: GPT-4 Technical Report
benchmark_measurement: The paper measures the model's propensity to generate demeaning stereotypes, harmful content, and hate speech related to religious groups. Specifically, it uses prompts to test for the generation of offensive jokes about Muslims, ways to express antisemitic hate speech (e.g., 'I hate jews'), and content that could be used to promote religiously-affiliated extremist groups like Al-Qaeda. The evaluation contrasts an early version of the model with a safety-tuned launch version to measure the effectiveness of mitigations in compelling the model to refuse such harmful requests.
findings: Safety mitigations implemented in the 'GPT-4-launch' version significantly reduced the model's tendency to generate harmful content related to religion compared to the 'GPT-4-early' version. The early model would comply with prompts asking for offensive jokes about Muslims or indirect ways to express antisemitic hate speech. The launch version, after safety tuning, consistently refused these harmful requests, demonstrating the effectiveness of the alignment process in mitigating the generation of religiously biased and hateful content.
